clue.text: Budget period lacking information provider

indicators.note: to lack something is to be without it, so one piece must be taken out of the other

blocks.note: a generation is a span of time, roughly thirty years
a gene carries genetic information, so it provides it

explanation.surface: A budget planned for some period that left out whoever supplied the data.
explanation.walkthrough: GENERATION loses GENE from its front, leaving RATION. 'Information provider' looks like a data company, but it is the gene of biology.
explanation.definitionFit: To ration something is to budget it, allowing out only a fixed limited share at a time.

clue.text: Dire roof needing repair, this might prevent disaster

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so these letters must be put back into a new working order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A house owner warned that a terrible roof should be fixed before catastrophe strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the roof the thing that saves the day, but the letters of DIRE ROOF rearrange into FIRE DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire door is built to resist flames and stop a blaze spreading, so it can stop a catastrophe.

clue.text: Author caught in Welsh town

indicators.note: to catch words is to hear them, so we want what is heard, not what is spelt

blocks.note: Barry is a seaside town in south Wales, near Cardiff

explanation.surface: A writer was arrested while visiting a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' reads as arrested, but here it means heard. J. M. Barrie wrote Peter Pan, and his name sounds just like the Welsh town.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie was the Scottish novelist and playwright best known for creating Peter Pan.

clue.text: Everyman is a former English footballer

blocks.note: the printed word splits in two, and each half is read separately in the blocks that follow
every one is all of them
a cock is a male bird, and 'old cock' is a matey British way to address a man

explanation.surface: A claim that some ex-England player is just an ordinary bloke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everyman' looks like one word, and is also the name of a rival crossword series, but it splits into Every and man. Terry Allcock played for Norwich City.
explanation.definitionFit: Terry Allcock was an English professional footballer who starred for Norwich City in the fifties and sixties.

clue.text: Singer turned up with coat, it was found over the road

definitions.text: it was found over the road

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up means it now reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: an informer who sings to the police is a rat
a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh

explanation.surface: A vocalist appeared wearing a coat that someone had found lying across the street.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'singer' is not a vocalist but an informer, a rat. 'It' in the definition is the stuff itself, laid over the road surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac is the asphalt surfacing spread on roads, so it lies on top of the roadway.

clue.text: Songbird exhausted eating each of ants at first

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied out, so only the shell of the word is kept
to eat something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the other
at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: the printed compound splits: its first half is the definition, its second half the bird used in the next block
the word emptied of its middle leaves only its ends
each of them means all of them
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tired songbird swallowing the first ant it comes across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Songbird' looks like one word, but 'Song' is the definition and 'bird' is wordplay; B and D go around ALL plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a song, usually slow and narrative or sentimental, telling a story in verse.

clue.text: Spartan friend at heart

blocks.note: Spartan means austere, plain and without frills
an ally is a friend or partner

explanation.surface: A warrior from ancient Sparta who is a comrade deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spartan' wants to be a citizen of Sparta, but here it is the lower-case adjective for frugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean fundamentally or in essence, describing what is true underneath the surface.

clue.text: Islander agreed in Munich to accompany vehicle

blocks.note: ja is German for yes, and Munich is in Germany
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An island native who said yes in Bavaria and went along with a car.
explanation.walkthrough: A foreign city signals a word in that country's language; here German for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Javan is a native or inhabitant of Java, the main island of Indonesia.

clue.text: Divert kids and react excitedly

indicators.note: excited things jump about, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent distracts the children, and they respond with great enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' here simply joins the two words whose letters are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidetrack someone is to turn their attention away from the main matter, to distract them.

clue.text: Blunt force ultimately shown by military, one sailor dismissed?

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is wanted
dismissed people are sent away, so these letters leave the word

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Blunt military force used, with one seaman discharged from service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunt' reads as an adjective for force, but it is the surname of the actress Emily Blunt; the question mark flags the trick. MILITARY loses I and TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Blunt is a British film actress, so her first name is defined by her surname.

clue.text: Family essentially returned to capital

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the middle of the word stays
returned means sent back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A household that basically went back to the big city.
explanation.walkthrough: The core of FAMILY, read backwards, gives LIMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru, on the Pacific coast of South America.

clue.text: Nancy’s in the Centre again

blocks.note: Nancy is a city in France, and the French word for in is en
the core is the centre of something

explanation.surface: A woman called Nancy is back at the community centre once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a woman's name, but it is the French city, so 'Nancy's in' is French for in.
explanation.definitionFit: Encore is a French word meaning once more, used in English as a call for a repeat.

clue.text: Officer content listening to match

indicators.note: listening attends to sound, so the word is taken as heard, not as spelt

blocks.note: CO is short for commanding officer
content is what is held within a container

explanation.surface: A police officer happily tuning in to a football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as happy, but it is the noun, what lies within. The second chunk sounds like INSIDE but is spelt to finish COINCIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things coincide when they agree or correspond exactly, the way matching items do.

clue.text: One-time British company involved in pharmaceutic industry

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be part of it, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A former British firm that worked in the drug business.
explanation.walkthrough: Imperial Chemical Industries really was a big British chemicals firm, so the surface is true.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial Chemical Industries was a major British chemical manufacturer, broken up and sold off in the 2000s.

clue.text: The cycling character

indicators.note: to cycle is to go round, so the final letter is moved round to the front

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reference to the one person on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: THE with its last letter brought to the front gives ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Eth is an Old English and Icelandic letter, so it is a written character of the alphabet.

clue.text: Extend beyond and above the knees

blocks.note: over means above
the lap is the top of the thighs when seated, just above the knees

explanation.surface: A skirt or coat whose hem reaches past and above the knees.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like describing a hemline; the knees are the lap of a seated person.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlap is to reach past an edge and cover part of something else.

clue.text: Product from well-limited stews

indicators.note: limited means cut back at its limits, so both edge letters go

blocks.note: to stew something is to boil it slowly
the inner letters once both ends are trimmed

explanation.surface: Something produced by stews kept within reasonable limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-limited' looks like one compound adjective; split it, and 'well' joins the definition while 'limited' trims the stews.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum is extracted by drilling and pumping, so crude from a drilled shaft is that shaft's output.

clue.text: Tense, absent from school for a long time

indicators.note: something absent is missing, so one letter is taken out

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English boarding school
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A nervous pupil who has skipped school for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as anxious, but it is the grammatical term, abbreviated to T.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immeasurably long period, an age.

clue.text: Native American ignoring a priest suffering

indicators.note: to ignore is to leave out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: the Apache are a Native American people
taken as written
P is an abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: A Native American who pays no heed to a clergyman in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: APACHE drops A and P from its front, leaving ACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is continuous dull pain, a form of physical distress or hurt.

clue.text: Pet and grope swimmer

blocks.note: a cat is a common household pet
to fish about is to grope or feel around for something

explanation.surface: Kissing and fondling someone, as an unruly date might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet and grope' reads as two verbs of fondling, but both are other senses: the noun pet and to fish about.
explanation.definitionFit: A catfish is a whiskered fish, and any fish can be called a swimmer in crosswords.

clue.text: Art school briefly enjoyable before travelling, not being old

indicators.note: briefly means in short form, so the word loses its last letter
not being means without, so the letter for old is removed

blocks.note: fun means enjoyable
tourism is travelling for pleasure

explanation.surface: A design college offers a quick good time before you set off on your journey.
explanation.walkthrough: FUN is shortened to FU, and TOURISM loses O, the standard abbreviation for old.
explanation.definitionFit: Futurism was an early twentieth-century Italian art movement celebrating speed, machines and modernity.

clue.text: Comes to by nurses

blocks.note: by and at both mean located near, as in 'at the door'
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: A patient regains consciousness thanks to the hospital staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes to' suggests waking up, but it means goes to, as with a meeting. 'Nurses' looks like hospital staff but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to go to it or be present there, so it means comes along.

clue.text: Outsider with sexy trousers?

blocks.note: longs is an informal word for long trousers
hot means sexy or attractive

explanation.surface: A rank outsider who nonetheless wears seductive trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Sexy trousers would be 'hot longs'; read as 'longs hot', the space shifts and the answer appears. The question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A long shot is a competitor with little chance of winning, just as a racing outsider is.

clue.text: Numbers of consecutive punches

blocks.note: first meaning: the first two counting numbers, said in sequence
second meaning: a boxer's quick jab followed straight away by a cross

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like counting a flurry of blows; the first numbers in order also name a boxing combination.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing a one-two is a rapid pair of blows, a jab and then a stronger cross.

clue.text: Girl suppressing a long hiccup

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down out of sight, so it is removed

blocks.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
taken as written
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A young woman trying to stifle a lengthy bout of hiccups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A long hiccup' reads as one phrase, but GAL loses A and then takes ITCH. 'Hiccup' is the definition in its figurative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup in plans is a minor setback, the same as a small fault or snag.

clue.text: When up this might conceal courage

blocks.note: first meaning: add 'up' and this verb means to keep feelings hidden
second meaning: British slang for nerve or daring

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic hint: add 'up' to the verb and it means to suppress emotions. In British slang, to lose your bottle is to lose your nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang bottle means nerve or daring, so someone with bottle is brave.

clue.text: Supporter against FA banning children in large republic

indicators.note: to ban is to shut out, so those letters are excluded

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all, which is zilch
CH is the standard abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: A fan opposing the Football Association's ban on young players in a big country.
explanation.walkthrough: FA looks like the Football Association, but here it is 'sweet FA', meaning nothing. ZILCH loses CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazil is the largest country in South America, and a federal republic.

clue.text: Hole up in sound mattress

indicators.note: sound means as heard, so the spoken form of the word is wanted

blocks.note: a Lilo is a British brand of inflatable air mattress

explanation.surface: Hiding away inside a decent mattress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' reads as healthy or solid, describing the mattress, but it flags how the word is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To hole up is to hide away and keep out of sight, the same as keeping a low profile.

clue.text: Finished once more supplying buttered, identical sandwiches

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between slices, so the letters lie within the words before it

blocks.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone made the same buttered sandwiches all over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like the food being made, but it is a verb meaning holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Redid is the past tense of redo, meaning did or completed again a second time.

clue.text: Couple again hands to those who put things right

blocks.note: to pair is to couple, and RE- means again
hands are workers, as in farmhands

explanation.surface: Reuniting a pair and passing them on to the fixers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' reads as a noun, but it is the verb to join, so coupling again is re-pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairmen are workers who mend broken things, setting faults right.

clue.text: Double top (which is checkout) easy for beginners

indicators.note: beginners are what start things, so only opening letters are taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Darts advice: double top, the double twenty, is a simple finish for novices.
explanation.walkthrough: In darts, double top is the double twenty segment and a checkout is the finishing throw. 'Double top' reads as one phrase, but 'Double' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Double as an adverb means two times over, so it can stand in for the answer.

clue.text: Son said: ‘I’m ordering for entrée’

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put in a new sequence

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: At a restaurant, a boy announces he is choosing the starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrée' looks like a course at dinner, but it is the French word for entry; 'ordering' is not choosing food.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrée means the right to enter, so admission to a club or place is a synonym.
